explanations.answer: They saw His signs on the sick
explanations.explanation: John 6:2 says the crowd followed Him "because they saw the signs He was performing on the sick." They'd watched people get healed, and they weren't about to miss the next one. I'd follow that too, friend. Nobody in that crowd was there for the scenery.

explanations.answer: He invited them to the mountain
explanations.explanation: The text never says Jesus invited anybody anywhere. It gives the reason straight out: the crowd followed because they saw the signs He was performing on the sick. In verse 3, Jesus goes up on the mountain with His disciples, and in verse 5 the crowd comes toward Him. The signs are what pulled them along.

John 6:2 doesn't mention any leaders sending anybody. This crowd came on their own, "because they saw the signs He was performing on the sick." That's the reason the text gives. They saw it with their own eyes and followed Him.

John 6:6 says it plainly: "He was asking this to test him, for He knew what He was about to do." Jesus wasn't short on ideas, and He wasn't lost. He already had the plan. I think Philip got handed a pop quiz with the answer key already in Jesus' pocket.

Verse 6 gives the reason for the question, and it isn't comfort. The text says Jesus asked "to test him, for He knew what He was about to do." Philip is one of His disciples, and the question was a test. The text doesn't say Philip needed soothing.

No warning in this one, friend. John 6:6 says Jesus was asking "to test him, for He knew what He was about to do." The question about buying bread was a test for Philip, one of His disciples. Jesus already knew where it was going.

That's the opposite of what Philip says. In John 6:7 he answers, "Two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for each of them to have a small piece." So even a small piece for everybody was out of reach. Philip, one of Jesus' disciples, ran the numbers and the numbers said no.

Right, the money doesn't stretch that far. Philip, one of Jesus' disciples, says in John 6:7, "Two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for each of them to have a small piece." Not a full portion. Not even a small piece for each person.

Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, says, "Here is a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish. But what difference will these make among so many?" (John 6:9). He spots what's on hand, then says out loud how small it looks next to that crowd. I think anybody would have asked the same thing. Hold onto that question, because it gets answered.

Andrew did ask it. He's one of the disciples, and Simon Peter's brother. After pointing out the boy's five barley loaves and two small fish, he says, "But what difference will these make among so many?" (John 6:9). He said the doubt right out loud.

John 6:11 says Jesus gave thanks and distributed to those seated "as much as they wanted." Five thousand men, and nobody got a ration. Then verse 12 says everyone was full. Philip's math about a small piece didn't get the last word.

A small piece was Philip's estimate back in verse 7, not what happened. John 6:11 says Jesus distributed to those seated "as much as they wanted." Then everyone was full, and there were leftovers on top of that. Philip, one of His disciples, had run the numbers, and they didn't cover this.

The text doesn't hand out portions like that. John 6:11 says Jesus distributed "as much as they wanted," and verse 12 says everyone was full. Twelve baskets of pieces were left over from the five barley loaves (John 6:13). That's no half loaf apiece.

Jesus says, "Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted" (John 6:12). Everybody's already full, and He still cares about the leftovers. The disciples collect them and fill twelve baskets. Not one crumb goes to waste.

The word in John 6:12 is a different one. Jesus tells His disciples, "Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted." The point is about not wasting what's left. Nobody was worried about pieces being forgotten.

Nobody in the text is watching for thieves. Jesus tells His disciples, "Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted" (John 6:12). The concern is waste. So they gather the pieces up, and the baskets fill.

explanations.answer: This is the Prophet who is to come
explanations.explanation: After they see the sign, the people begin to say, "Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world" (John 6:14). They'd just eaten as much as they wanted from a boy's lunch. I think that'd get my attention too. And the sign isn't the end of it, since verse 15 shows what the crowd does next.

explanations.answer: This is Elijah come back to them
explanations.explanation: John 6:14 doesn't name anybody like that. What the people begin to say is, "Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world." That's the title the text gives. They'd just seen the sign with the loaves.

explanations.answer: This is a new teacher of the law
explanations.explanation: The crowd says something bigger than that. In John 6:14 they begin to say, "Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world." They were reacting to the sign Jesus had performed. Nobody calls Him a teacher of the law in this passage.

explanations.answer: Withdraws to a mountain by Himself
explanations.explanation: John 6:15 says Jesus realized they were about to come and make Him king by force, so He "withdrew again to a mountain by Himself." The crowd wanted to crown Him, and He walked away from it. The text doesn't tell us why He chose that. It just tells us what He did.

explanations.answer: Sends the crowd away to the villages
explanations.explanation: That's not what the text says He did. John 6:15 says Jesus "withdrew again to a mountain by Himself." The text doesn't mention Him sending the crowd anywhere. He was the one who left.

explanations.answer: Lets them take Him to Jerusalem
explanations.explanation: The crowd never gets the chance. John 6:15 says Jesus realized they were about to make Him king by force, and He "withdrew again to a mountain by Himself." So He left before they could come for Him. Nobody takes Him anywhere in this part of the story.

John 6:17 says the disciples got into a boat and started across the sea, and "Jesus had not yet gone out to them." So He wasn't aboard. Verse 15 had Him on a mountain by Himself. The disciples set off without Him.

That's right. The text says the disciples got into a boat and started across the sea, and "Jesus had not yet gone out to them" (John 6:17). He wasn't in the boat when they set out. He was still on the mountain.

John 6:19 says they saw Jesus "approaching the boat, walking on the sea" and they were terrified. It was dark, the wind was strong, and then somebody comes walking toward you over the water. Friend, I'd have dropped my oar and probably my apron too. They had every reason to be rattled.

They're not calm at all. John 6:19 says they saw Jesus "approaching the boat, walking on the sea," and they were terrified. It was already dark, with a strong wind blowing. Then comes the line that settles them, in verse 20.

explanations.answer: It's Him and not to be afraid
explanations.explanation: Jesus speaks up: "It is I; do not be afraid" (John 6:20). He tells them who it is and tells them to set the fear down. Terrified men in a dark boat get four plain words. That's all it takes.

explanations.answer: To row harder for the shore
explanations.explanation: Jesus gives no rowing orders here. What He says is, "It is I; do not be afraid" (John 6:20). He tells them who He is and tells them not to fear. The disciples had already rowed three or four miles.

explanations.answer: To keep quiet and hold on tight
explanations.explanation: Nothing about keeping quiet or holding on. John 6:20 says Jesus spoke up: "It is I; do not be afraid." He told them who was coming toward the boat. He told them not to be afraid.

explanations.answer: They take Him in and land at once
explanations.explanation: John 6:21 says, "Then they were willing to take Him into the boat, and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading." The fear goes first, and then they take Him in. And the shore shows up right away. After all that rowing, I'd call that a nice finish.

explanations.answer: They row the rest of the night to land
explanations.explanation: The text has a much faster ending. John 6:21 says they were willing to take Jesus into the boat, "and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading." There's no long row left. They had been rowing before this, but the landing came at once.

explanations.answer: They turn the boat back toward the crowd
explanations.explanation: The boat keeps going the way it was headed. John 6:21 says they took Jesus into the boat, "and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading." Back in verse 17, they had started across the sea to Capernaum. They land at the place they were heading.
